executiveSummary: Deterministic Research Pipeline seam checks passed. findings.title: Delegation does not expose a child RunHandle
findings.description: Delegation lacked a public child RunHandle for inject/steer/wait.
findings.observedConsequence: Callers could not target delegated workers through the public API.

findings.title: Steering targets the supervisor rather than delegated worker
findings.description: Steering applied to the supervisor instead of the delegated worker.
findings.observedConsequence: Worker-targeted inject/steer could not be expressed publicly.
findings.workaround: Resolved via child-targeted control on ChildRunHandle (#249).

action.summary: Route inject/steer to the child run when a child handle is resolved.

action.summary: Apply Restart to eligible Other RunFailed; keep budget/max-steps terminal.

findings.title: Default LlmWatcher prompt leaves abort authority unscoped
findings.description: The default watcher prompt asks the model to review events and choose an action but states no boundary for `abort`, so a live model decides on its own what counts as abort-worthy. A delegation whose text named the failing fault_trigger tool was judged a prompt injection and aborted the drill run.
findings.observedConsequence: An operator-authorized fault drill was vetoed by the watcher before the restart path became observable, in 2 of 4 pre-repair live attempts; consumers have no documented policy for what a watcher may abort.
findings.workaround: Demos that need a long-running drill to finish scope their watcher prompt explicitly (see FAULT_DRILL_WATCHER_PROMPT); deterministic coverage uses scripted watchers.

action.summary: Document or bound watcher abort authority in the default prompt, and keep drill-shaped runs pre-scoped.

verification.summary: Observed in the pre-repair live attempts; the drill repair removes the veto for the demo but does not change the default prompt.
